column3: The Hebrew says “beyond the Jordan” and uses singular collective names for the peoples; BSB specifies “west of the Jordan” and uses plural ethnic names.
The Hebrew adds “one mouth” to their gathering for battle; BSB omits that image.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “and now” and uses the image of cutting a covenant; BSB has “please” and “make a treaty.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “man of Israel” and “the Hivite,” followed by singular “me” and “I”; BSB uses plural “men,” “Hivites,” “us,” and “we.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they came for the LORD’s “name” and repeats the hearing root in hearing His report; BSB has “fame” and “heard the reports about Him.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite” and simply says Og was “in Ashtaroth”; BSB has plural “Amorites” and supplies “reigned.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “all” the inhabitants and their “hand” for carrying provisions, and says “and now”; BSB omits “all” and the hand image and has “Please.”
The Hebrew has plural “our houses”; BSB says “at home.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the men simply “the men” and names the LORD’s “mouth”; BSB supplies “of Israel” and says “the counsel of the LORD.”
The Hebrew separately says Joshua made peace and cut a covenant; BSB combines this as “made a treaty of peace.”
The Hebrew leaves both parties unnamed and uses singular collective pronouns for Israel; BSB explicitly names “the Gibeonites” and “the Israelites” and uses plural “them.”
The Hebrew repeats “their cities” before listing them; BSB lists the names without repeating that phrase.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says the leaders spoke “to all the congregation”; BSB leaves the recipients implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they became woodcutters and water drawers “as the leaders had spoken to them”; BSB includes the service in the leaders’ command and then says they “kept their promise.”
The Hebrew calls the recipients “them” and has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB names “the Gibeonites” and gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew uses the image of a servant not being “cut off from among you”; BSB expresses this as serving perpetually.
The Hebrew leaves the speakers unnamed, explicitly names Joshua, and repeats “the land” in its inhabitants clause; BSB names “The Gibeonites,” leaves Joshua implicit, and uses “its inhabitants.”
The Hebrew has singular “your hand” and says “in your eyes”; BSB has plural “your hands” and “seems ... to you.”
The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he,” has singular “the hand of the sons of Israel,” and ends with “them”; BSB names Joshua, uses plural “hands,” and explicitly names the Gibeonites.
The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua and says “for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD”; BSB uses “he” and attaches “of the LORD” to “congregation.”
